query: Help me understand the key points in this table — what should I concentrate on?

per_column.name: crew_service_quality
per_column.rationale: Turning free-text into a qualitative crew taxonomy (warm_attentive / indifferent / rude / professional_neutral) gives a real grouping axis beyond the numeric 'Staff Service' score, e.g. isolating 'rude' cases. But groundedness is weak: only 40 NULLs across ~8100 rows means it labels almost every row, and sample 2 (a review purely about narrow seats and bad IFE, silent on crew) is confidently tagged 'indifferent' — an inference the text does not support. Warm/attentive labels on samples 1,3,4,5 are well warranted.

per_column.name: food_quality_assessment
per_column.rationale: A qualitative food axis is analytically useful and the large NULL bucket (3002) shows appropriate 'not stated' behaviour for many silent rows. However it still fabricates on silent rows in the samples: sample 2 mentions no food yet is 'poor', and sample 5 (only seats and movies mentioned) is 'adequate'. Where food IS discussed (samples 1,3,4 'excellent') the reading is sound.

per_column.name: proactive_service_frequency
per_column.rationale: Frequency of proactive service is a plausibly distinct angle, though it partly overlaps conceptually with crew_service_quality. Groundedness is the main problem: only 17 NULLs means it assigns a level to virtually every row, including sample 2 which says nothing about service cadence yet is scored 'minimal_reactive'. Samples with explicit 'crew came round regularly' (sample 4) are correctly 'frequent_proactive'.

per_column.name: seat_comfort_issue
per_column.rationale: Adds specific failure-type detail (cramped_or_narrow vs broken_or_faulty) that the raw numeric 'Seat Comfort' rating cannot give, useful for pinpointing what to concentrate on. Values track the text well: sample 2 'far too narrow, poor padding' -> cramped_or_narrow, sample 1 'spacious legroom' -> comfortable, and it uses NULL (4009) for silent rows correctly.

per_column.name: complaint_resolution_quality
per_column.rationale: Service-recovery outcome is a genuinely new axis not present in any original column and directly relevant to 'what to focus on'. The dominant 'not_applicable' bucket is the correct default when no complaint is described, and all five samples (none describing a complaint) are correctly 'not_applicable'.

per_column.name: communication_failure
per_column.rationale: A single boolean flag carries less analytical leverage than the multi-level columns, but it captures a specific, meaningful failure mode (communication breakdowns) that is distinct from the ratings and useful to filter on. All sampled rows are correctly 'False' with no communication issue described, indicating sound grounding on the visible evidence.

judge.rationale: For an open-ended 'what should I concentrate on' query, the added columns convert unstructured review text into several usable categorical/boolean axes (crew tone, food quality, seat issue type, complaint resolution, communication failures) that let an analyst group and compare beyond the raw numeric ratings. Redundancy is modest and acceptable. The recurring weakness is groundedness on rows where the source is silent: crew_service_quality, proactive_service_frequency, and (less often) food_quality_assessment almost never emit NULL and confidently label attributes the text never mentions — sample 2, a seats-only review, is nonetheless assigned crew, food, and service-frequency verdicts. seat_comfort_issue, complaint_resolution_quality, and communication_failure behave correctly, using appropriate 'not applicable'/NULL/false defaults and reading present evidence soundly.
